description:
MEASURED s505 (Fable, 2026-10-03) on the s501t tree 4fe06650 (#155 tie on ARRAY/HASH), ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s505/review/cost-onetie.pl (a container-heavy loop: hash stores, push, keys, element reads, exists, whole-container copies, delete, shift; run twice with no tie, twice with ONE unrelated `tie my %dummy, "Tie::StdHash"` alive, once after untie; sweep running beside it, so +-10 %):
  PCL  no tie 0.146 0.142 s | one live tie 0.215 0.198 s | after untie 0.159 s  => ratio 1.43
  PCL  no tie 0.155 0.147 s | one live tie 0.225 0.192 s | after untie 0.162 s  => ratio 1.38
  perl no tie 0.702 0.771 s | one live tie 0.758 0.727 s                        => ratio 1.01
So a program that never ties pays nothing measurable (the bench A/B of s501t: no row above the control band), and a program with ANY live container tie pays about +40 % on its UNTIED containers -- still ~3.5x faster than perl on this loop, and before #155 such a program printed wrong answers, so this did not block the merge.  It is a round candidate by measured gain for the population that ties (Env, Tie::RefHash, Tie::File, Tie::IxHash users).

WHY: `%p-tied` is `(and (plusp **p-tie-count**) (gethash c **p-tie-table**))` and the table is a WEAK EQ table (address-hashed, GC-aware: every lookup is the slow path).  With the count above zero EVERY census site (docs/tie-aggregates.md section 3: every hash STORE, push / shift / keys / flatten / copy entry, every element-read MISS) does that lookup for every container.

CANDIDATE (one macro, measure first): a tied container is by construction an EMPTY SHELL -- the design`s own invariant -- so `%p-tied` can refuse a non-empty container before the table: hash-table with count > 1 (a blessed shell keeps its one :__class__ entry) or a vector with length > 0 => not tied.  Then only empty containers reach the weak table.  Check before building: (1) the one documented exception, %p-sig-arg-avail, writes a tied @_ shell`s storage only BEYOND its fill pointer, so LENGTH stays 0; (2) %p-tied is also handed non-containers (%p-tie-views maps it over arbitrary list items) -- the pre-test must type-dispatch, never call LENGTH on a box; (3) the failure mode changes: a path that wrongly writes INTO a shell would make the tie invisible instead of half-working -- add a debug assertion at untie time (shell still empty) so the gate would see it.  Alternative if (3) is unwelcome: a non-weak EQ table plus explicit removal at untie (the weak table exists so a dropped tied container does not leak its record; perl has the same lifetime through DESTROY-less magic) -- measure both.
Bar: cost-onetie.pl ratio near 1.0; tools/bench-exec.pl rows arrhash hashcopy slices sortnum tiehash unchanged inside the control band; Pl/t/tie-aggregate-01.t + the companion tie files unchanged.


=== DONE (s507p, Opus, 2026-10-05; worktree agent-a55609aa75faa5780) ===
SHIPPED: %p-tied asks %p-tie-shell-shape-p (an empty vector, or a hash of at most its blessing key) BEFORE the weak table; untie checks the shell is empty (%p-tie-check-shell-empty dies naming it).  INVARIANT verified: an audit build logging any tied container with non-empty storage at every %p-tied site logged nothing over the tie Pl/t files, the s505 probe set and 10 companion tie files; by reading, tie empties the shell, %p-sig-arg-avail writes only past the fill pointer, local on an aggregate rebinds.
Numbers: cost-onetie ratio (one live tie / none) base 1.36 / 1.48 / 1.48 -> 0.99 / 1.10 / 1.01 (perl 1.06), sums same; bench tiehash 0.2943 -> 0.2288 s (-22.3 %, ctl -0.7); no untied row above the band.  `use English` (live SCALAR ties) never cost untied containers, on fee16466 or after (cost-english-1.log): scalar ties do not touch **p-tie-count**.  Guard Pl/t/perf-levers-08.t rows 2, 4, 9.
subject: perf: ONE live container tie costs every UNTIED container about +40 % (the weak-table lookup behind %p-tied at every census site); candidate: refuse a non-empty container before the table -- a tied container is always an empty shell
